title: Minimax Rate for Functional Difference-in-Differences in a Designed Sparse-Visit Benchmark
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4; not salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves a same-class expected-supremum bracket with lower logarithmic power 2/15 and upper power 2/7, so only the polynomial factor (n^2m)^(-2/15) is matched.

It does not determine the exact logarithmic minimax rate or the logarithm-refined crossover with the scalar n^(-2/7) floor, and its framing correctly leaves both open rather than claiming a sharp full rate.

The contribution is confined to a calibrated benchmark with a fixed known visit-density family, uniform control covariates, dimension ten, and m <= n^(1/7), which prevents flagship breadth despite the nonroutine estimator and converse.
paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier field is capped at subfield.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved a fixed-n correlated-sign converse, a split-subject upper construction, and a positive logarithmic lower penalty under the recorded visit design; the math referee passed. D0.5 graded the resulting same-class polynomial-rate bracket subfield because the exact logarithmic minimax factor and refined crossover remain open within a narrow designed benchmark. A field-tier continuation needs a new bounded construction for that logarithmic gap or a broader re-anchored model; the Abadie (2005) positioning sentence also remains to be repaired in any follow-on paper.
tldr: This designed and calibrated two-period functional DiD benchmark fixes both the reference target population and a bounded recorded visit-density family before sampling. For exactly \(n\) independent subjects and \(m\) visits per period, the observable split-subject estimator and the fixed-\(n\) correlated-sign converse give the polynomial expected-supremum minimax rate \((n^2m)^{-2/15}\) for \(1\leq m\leq n^{1/7}\). Conditional on realized covariates and visits, exact Gaussian mark factorization and the uniform bound \(\int \kappa_{r,\delta}^2f_{10}\leq (2/3)C_f\delta\) make the converse valid for the common prespecified, possibly nonuniform visit design. The multilocation construction further proves the lower logarithmic power \(2/15\), while the observable upper theorem has power \(2/7\). Thus a positive logarithmic penalty is unavoidable, but its exact power remains open. At \(m\asymp n^{1/7}\), the polynomial factor equals the scalar \(n^{-2/7}\) floor while the logarithmic lower bound already exceeds it, so the logarithm-refined elbow is not identified.
gap: Existing functional-outcome regression and event-study inference furnish simultaneous bands for observed curves or sufficiently dense interpolated panels, functional DiD inference presumes reconstruction negligible at the root-\(n\) scale, sparse functional mean theory omits confounding, and scalar higher-order theory omits the repeated-visit channel and curve supremum loss; none supplies a minimax theorem for the literal prespecified reference-population and visit-randomization protocol studied here.
fill: A same-class upper and lower theorem exposes the asymmetric density-versus-visit information product for this calibrated protocol, supplies an observable reconstruction-free estimator robust to independent finite-variance measurement errors, and certifies the subject-level likelihood converse on a Gaussian least-favorable submodel.
